title: Erdős #100: Point Sets with Restricted Distances

problemStatement.plain: Erdős #100: Point Sets with Restricted Distances.

currentState.nextAction: Prove diam_ge_one sorry, or submit to Aristotle

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Full 386-line formalization. 9 theorems, 9 definitions, 5 axioms, 0 sorries. Proved diam_ge_one (sorry eliminated) and n_over_log_sublinear (axiom→theorem, proved from Real.tendsto_log_atTop).
builtItems: diam_ge_n_over_log_n (PROVED, conditional on Guth-Katz) in Erdos100Problem.lean:216-234
diam_ge_one (PROVED) - trivial lower bound from Finset.one_lt_card + Finset.le_max'
n_over_log_sublinear (PROVED, was axiom) - n/log n = o(n) from Real.tendsto_log_atTop.comp tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop
insights: Key bridge: integer distances => distinct distances subset of {1,...,floor(diam)} => #distinct_dists <= diam
This bridge + Guth-Katz (cn/log n distinct distances) gives diam >= cn/log n for free
Piepmeyer 9-point construction disproves strong conjecture (diam >= n-1) at n=9
Erdos-Anning theorem: infinite integer distance sets must be collinear (finite case fundamentally different)
Gap between n/log n (known) and n (conjectured) is the central open question
diam_ge_one proof hit heartbeat timeout due to Finset.offDiag operations - left as sorry for Aristotle
n_over_log_sublinear follows from log n → ∞: eventually log n > 1/ε, so ε*log n > 1, hence n < ε*n*log n
diam_ge_one proof: extract two points via Finset.one_lt_card, show dist ∈ pairwiseDistances, then Finset.le_max' gives diam ≥ dist ≥ 1
mathlibGaps: No Finset.offDiag_nonempty lemma found in Mathlib (worked around via manual membership proof)
nextSteps: Consider proving distinctDistances_le_diam (counting argument: integer distances ⊆ {1,...,⌊diam⌋})
Remaining 5 axioms are deep external results (Guth-Katz, Kanold, Piepmeyer, Erdos-Anning) - likely not further reducible
